correctness.rationale: For arbitrary compact nonnegative initial trait measure, full-line Gaussian characteristic representation gives exact MGF (1), conditional variance V=K0''(A)+Dt, positive finite-time existence via m<=L0+D k s0 t^2/2, bounded compartments and mass conservation. For D>0 s_infty>0 would force m>=m0+(kDs_infty/2)t^2, making log i grow unbounded despite i<=1. Since integral i=(r_infty-r0)/mu finite and limits exist, i_infty=0, s_infty=0 and r_infty=1. For D=0 or any conservative [0,L] mutation, m<=L yields s_infty>=s0 exp[-k L(1-r0)/mu]>0. A two-point initial mixture proves assumptions do not require Gaussian data; standalone exact arithmetic checker verifies transform polynomial identity but does not prove infinite time.

value.rationale: The source interprets λ as a contagion probability but uses diffusion on an effectively unbounded trait line. Showing that any D>0 then forces all susceptibles to disappear for arbitrary compact starting data, whereas a genuine probability cap yields an explicit strictly positive survivor fraction, is a mathematically motivated and substantial distinction between finite-horizon approximations and infinite-time conclusions. The non-Gaussian variance identity and explicit D=0 jump are reproducible structural information, not a textbook rearrangement or arbitrary numerical slice. It does not imply real-world universal infection.
